text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony 950 Touch IR Remote Control - Discontinued by Manufacturer Logitech makes the best universal remote controls and they keep introducing new models that are better and better. If you have half a dozen (or more) remote controls on your living room table and are always losing some of them or forgetting which does what, then a universal remote is for you.

The Harmony 950 appears to be mostly the same as the Harmony Elite, except without the Harmony Hub device. The Harmony Hub can be purchased separately later, though the Elite package is cheaper if you're getting it anyway. The Harmony Hub greatly expands the range and capabilities of your Harmony remote, so you should think twice before skipping it.

Logitech also sells much cheaper Harmony remotes without the touch screen. The main benefit of the touch screen is to program shortcuts to your favorite TV channels and to control more devices than the non-touch remote controls can access. If you always use your DVR or cable box's on-screen channel menu and only have a few devices, then maybe a much cheaper Harmony without the touch screen is a better value for you.

The Harmony is pretty easy to program by connecting to your PC and connecting to the Logitech website. If you have an older Harmony remote, you may be able to transfer all your device settings to this one. The buttons on the Harmony are easy to see, well spaced and give you good feedback when pressed.

Battery life is OK for a touchscreen device, but like your smartphone you will need to recharge this at least every couple of days. Most people will leave the Harmony in the recharging station most of the time, so make sure you have an electrical outlet close to where you will be using the Harmony.

If you're in the market for a universal remote, Logitech Harmony should be first on your list. The only decision you have to make is which model to buy. If you're trying to control a handful of devices (TV, cable box, DVR, stereo system, game system, DVD player), then you really have to ask yourself if the touchscreen feature is worth the big price premium. If you have a "smart home" with remote controlled lights, outlets, thermostat, etc or if your devices are spread around a large room so the IR remote has trouble connecting with them, then the Harmony Hub is a good idea.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony 950 Touch IR Remote Control - Discontinued by Manufacturer

text_fidelity_a:
MOSISO Fashion Laptop Backpack for Women, Pure Deep Gray I am in love with this bag!
It has so many features that are important to me.
I plan on using this bag for day trips with the family and especially during my childrens' swim meets.
This bag has more compartments and zippers then I expected it to have.
There are three main large compartments, two small compartments in the front and an anti-theft pocket in the back and the side water bottle mesh are also contained in a pocket. I was a little worried that I wouldn't be able to fit my water bottle in the outside mesh since there is a zipper and extra fabric and stuff, but as you can see from my image, a sports drink bottle fits perfectly in there.
The bag comes with its own lock which can be programmed to your own code.
The bag has two padded sections within the two largest zippered areas. One for a laptop with a velcro strip and one in the middle section with no velcro.
I plan to use the middle padded area for my mp3 player as this is the area that the headphone cables enter into and I will also put my power bank in that padded area since this is also where the charger port comes from.
The color of this bag is very modern, it's a good bag for a male or female.
I like that I can zip shut the drink compartments if I wanted to have something in them that I don't want to fall out (skittles/sunflower seeds)!
There is a padded carry handle and a non-padded hanging handle which is really nice. The back is very padded as are the shoulder straps.
There is even a luggage strap for if I wanted to bring this on the plane trip.
There are two cinch straps above each water bottle which is nice, as sometimes I like to cinch in my jacket or if I had a lot of bulky stuff inside that could be cinched to remove air and the bulk.
The bag has the interior organization in the front large compartment, including a clip for your keys, two wider sections, mesh on one and two pencil holes, which is great for me as I like to bring a pencil, sharpie, and highlighter with me to the swim meets.
I like that there are so many large compartments, allowing me to keep my stuff separate. I like to bring magazines to read between heats and sometimes my laptop (rear), snacks in the middle and the schedule and journal in the front.
I like the smaller compartment to contain the emergency kit (bandaids, pain reliever, etc).
I don't think there is anything else in a bag that this bag doesn't have.
A great mom bag!
text_fidelity_b: MOSISO Fashion Laptop Backpack for Women, Pure Deep Gray

text_fidelity_a:
Brainwavz M1 in-Ear Noise Isolating Earphones While these don’t offer the sound quality of higher-end Brainwavz buds (or higher-end models from other brands), the sound quality and overall performance is quite good for the price point, and the comfort is excellent.

The best description I can offer of the sound quality is “clean.” The upper and mid ranges come through very clearly and are far more well-defined than typical with budget/value earbuds. The bass is not pronounced. It’s there, but it’s not what I’d describe as punchy. These are not an ideal set if you’re looking for head-thumping bass.

The comfort is typical for Brainwavz, which is to say it’s excellent. There’s a variety of ear tips so you can customize the fit to your ear. I’m especially fond of the Comply foam tips since they provide a great (but still comfortable) seal. That helps maintain good sound isolation and also helps with the bass response. It also helps keep the earbuds in place while exercising.

The cords are thin but seem sturdy enough for typical use. The same for the ear buds themselves. While they don’t have as solid of a build quality as higher-priced models, I don’t get the feeling that these will be falling apart anytime soon. That being said, it would have been nice to have more reinforcement where the cord meets the earbud, since that’s a prime stress point in use (even though these come with a very well made carry case, more often than not I just wind them around whatever device I am using).

For the price these are hard to beat. Highly recommend these as a not too expensive way to substantially upgrade from the stock earbuds that come with many devices.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Brainwavz M1 in-Ear Noise Isolating Earphones

text_fidelity_a: Jabra SUPREME Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging - Black I had always found the Motorola H700 flip headset to be the best and most convenient bluetooth solution. Its performance was good and  the flip microphone made it easy to carry in a holster. Unfortunately it finally died and they are out of production. So I decided to try this headset and was pleasantly surprised. This actually surpasses the Motorola H700. Voice recognition by my iPhone is improved - presumably because of the better noise reduction of the headset, the calls seem very clear on both ends, and the talking caller ID is a real plus.It can fit in the same holster I used for my H700 - though it is a bit large for it. If I can find a holster with a belt clip, this could be a real winner. The only con is that it isn't extremely comfortable on the earlobe after a few hours. The bar that holds the ear clip to the unit is a bit too long I think and the end poking through tends to be a little irritating. It comes with an additional ear pad and clip but there is not really any more comfort using either of those. I have not tried the "comfort kit" - sold separately for way too much money. When I first saw the "comfort kit" advertised I was amused that a $100 bluetooth headset would need an additional expenditure  to be comfortable. However I may be forced to try it if I can't get  the ear clip adjusted properly. Jabra should be embarrassed by this.

text_fidelity_a:
Klipsch GiG Black Portable Speaker, Black I really wanted to like this speaker. It comes complete with international plugs, an a/c wall charger, and two pouches which I assume is one for the unit and one for the accessories. It is somewhat attractive with a built-in stand that allows you to either place it on its side or in an upright position.

With most speakers, once you have paired it with your device (an Iphone 5s, in my case), you should be all done. This is not so with this unit. The speaker has a spring-loaded slide switch that you push on. It gives you a guitar confirmation tone so that you know that it's working. Now you must go to the "Settings" icon on your device and manually choose the Klipsch speaker. Then you will hear another guitar confirmation tone letting you know that it is paired. You must do this EVERY SINGLE TIME. It is ridiculous. Of course when you turn it off, it will give you yet another guitar confirmation tone.

The sound is very good, but the extra step of always having to re-enable the bluetooth connection through "Settings" totally negates anything positive about this speaker. There is absolutely no reason why my Sony SRSX5 and my JBL Charge automatically pair with my device whenever I turn them on, and yet this one does not. I keep trying to understand why the developers came up with this procedure, but it totally baffles me.

I know that other users have complained in the past about charging issues. Perhaps Klipsch listened to them and fixed this problem because I have not had any difficulties with that.

If you're gonna spend money on a good speaker, please look at the Sony SRSX5. It is an outstanding speaker with logical functions and exceptional sound.
text_fidelity_b: Klipsch GiG Black Portable Speaker, Black

Do yourself a favor and skip the included sofware. It was useless bloatware in my case. FYI, I had to go into "services" in both versions of Windows 7 I've tried this on, and turn both bluetooth services to automatic to have this pick up by itself.

Surprisingly, if you turn this off on one computer, it must set a bit inside the device, because it will then stay off if you move it to another computer, and - in my case - I had to move it back to the first computer to turn it back on before it would work.

Marware Revolve Portrait and Landscape Standing Case for Kindle Fire HD 8.9", Black (will not fit HDX models) I have 3 covers and this is by far my favorite. It was hard to get the Kindle in the plastic holder at first but then I got it in and it will hold even if I throw it across the room,not that I would. In the land scape position there are three notches to get just the right angle for you. You can also rotate it, so it stands up in the portrait position.
Things to keep in mind. You want to make sure the plastic holder is rotated in the right position before you put the Kindle in. You want to make sure the opening for the speakers line up but that also, the USB port for charging is going to be on the outside so you can close the case when you are charging. I didn't have it lined up correctly and at first I though it was a design flaw, until I realized I could rotate the holder all the way around.
It is a nice soft leather, with an elastic band to hold the case closed. These features make it the best one I've seen yet, very sturdy and versatile and nice looking.

Of course almost every peripheral I use is USB 2.0/3.0, so I have adapters everywhere and can never find one when I need it, or don’t have enough ports to plug in everything I want to use.

So this USB C Hub from Flagtop is super handy to have around. I use it to connect a second monitor (HDMI port), an external mouse/keyboard (USB 2.0 ports), and the power cable (USB C port).

I like that the USB 2.0/USB 3.0 ports have a little space between each one. This makes them usable even if you have a thick thumb drive or cable plugged in.

I had to have the ports on my laptop replaced because they loosened up over time, so I like that I can reduce wear on the new ports by unplugging the hub to disconnect everything.

The port runs warm. It’s hot to the touch; my desk feels warm underneath it.

I do wish the cable for the hub was longer. If I have my laptop on a stand, the hub dangles from one of the ports. The cable is about 5.5 inches, and if I have several things plugged into it, I feel like that’s a lot of weight to have hanging off a single port on the side of my laptop.
text_fidelity_b: FLAGTOP 7 in 1 USB C Hub for Universal Devices, Support 4K HDMI/PD 3.0 / USB 3.0 / 2USB 2.0 / SD/Micro SD/TF, USB Type C Dongle Hub (02A)

text_fidelity_a:
HP ENVY Photo 7155 All-in-One Photo Printer (K7G93A) and XL Ink Cartridges - 4 Colors This is a multi-functional unit. It scans, prints (papers and photos), and does copies. It has two media trays; one can load 8-1/2x11 paper, and photo paper in the second tray. Prints are of very high quality. I printed beautiful pictures and crisp email messages from my laptop in the living room. You can use the same tray for either 5x7 or 4x6 photo papers. I tried to print separately using my personal computer or work computer, they worked well except that this printer did not work with my chromebook. HP gave a message saying that this printer does not support Chromebook. I could not connect wirelessly to my work laptop, only with USB cables. But my personal computer linked wirelessly. The installation is simple, but took an awful lot of time to download HP programs to get the printer going. This printer also supports mobile printing with iPhone, but I did not try that feature. Another feature that I didn’t have in my previous printer is the use of SD card to print quality pictures. The machine has a SD card port and you can insert the card and print effortlessly. The touch screen interface is easy to operate the printer, but first you need to get familiar with it

Other cons are that it does not have built-in fax capability, and does not have Ethernet network interfaces, which may be an additional feature some users may be looking. Such a feature is an ideal choice for printer sharing with your family or the home office or for business. It is a little heavy and an average size printer. I did not sign up for the "HP Instant Ink" program. You have the choice not to sign up if you don’t want it. But if you are planning on this option, make sure that if you sign up and then cancel your subscription anytime, the printer will not get disabled. I have rated this product three stars for overall satisfaction.
text_fidelity_b: HP ENVY Photo 7155 All-in-One Photo Printer (K7G93A) and XL Ink Cartridges - 4 Colors

text_fidelity_a: Lenovo Chromebook C330 2-in-1 Convertible Laptop, 11.6" HD Display, MediaTek MT8173C, 4GB RAM, 64GB Storage, Chrome OS, Blizzard White Chromebook prices range from around $100 to over $1000. Better Chromebooks have Intel Core CPUs for great performance. The much cheaper Mediatek system in this Chromebook gives it mediocre performance, especially for intensive games or for business users who open lots of tabs simultaneously and frequently switch between them. On the plus side this Chromebook has a useful 4GB of RAM, a sharp colorful IPS screen, a touch screen that works great with Android apps, a very responsive (for swiping) touchpad, and reliable WiFi (much better than my HP laptop). On the minus side, the white plastic shell looks and feels a little cheap, the screen is not very bright, and the touchpad's button feels a little clunky. In summary, if you can't afford more than $300, this is a good choice for casual users who only have a few tabs open at once and use it mostly for email, Facebook, web surfing, and streaming music or videos. If you can afford $350 to $400, you will have several choices with more powerful CPUs for more intensive users.
text_fidelity_b: Lenovo Chromebook C330 2-in-1 Convertible Laptop, 11.6" HD Display, MediaTek MT8173C, 4GB RAM, 64GB Storage, Chrome OS, Blizzard White

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation I just unpackaged and started using the Amazon Fire TV. Right off I had to do a small update which didn't take long at all. Next there is a neat video that shows you how to use the device. I think this is the first time I have had a video box teach me how to use it with a video. It is a nice touch.

I'm already a prime member, but for those who are not the video spoke of a 30 days trial.

Right off the bat I noticed in the main menu of items to choose from that there are movies, tv, watchlist, video library, games, apps, photo and settings. What's missing from this is the Amazon Music of which I have quite a few albums. I hope we get to see music in some future update. That's kind of a glaring omission in my opion. One star knocked off for that right there.

One cool feature I noted right off the bat is that the device already knows me. I didn't have to log in or do anything.

The watchlist

So I went straight to my watchlist to confirm that it indeed already knows me. It does. And I went to a recent season of shows I am watching where the first two episodes have been watched and the third has not. There is a white bar at the bottom of those watched and missing from the one that is yet to be watched. So I'll guess that is my progress bar as well. Nice touch.

Voice feature

This feature is slightly confusing to me right off. What you do is hold the mic button down until you hear a tone, then continue to hold it down as you speak your question or title search. When you are done talking, only then do you release the button. I kept letting it go as soon as I heard the tone, which causes it to attempt to process the question. So the feature is a little odd, but once you get used to that oddity it works quite well.

I asked it, "what's new this week" and got three suggestions. I further asked it questions like, show me my watchlist which offered me two methods, "watch list" and "watchlist". Neither of which showed me my actual watchlist. Clearly the audio search isn't yet fully aware of navigation.

Purchasing a TV show

Photos

Looks like they have an iOS and Android app that lets you share photos with Amazon Cloud Drive and thus have them available on this device. I'll have to try that out. I'll skip it for now.

Apps

This looks good for now. NetFlix and Pandora are here as well as Hulu. I use all three of those so that's good.

Games

There are good looking games here. I didn't buy the game controller as I own a console already, but I might rethink that.

YouTube

I didn't see YouTube, so I did a voice search and an app popped up. Once the app downloaded and installed, I had to visit an activation page of YouTube to connect it to the device. Very simple and now I have YouTube on here.

NetFlix

Netflix didn't have a simple activate system. I had to punch in my email and password via the remote. Boo! In this era of complex passwords, activation should become a standard function on TV based media devices.

Navigation

The navigation is quite smooth. I guess thanks to some good specs under the hood. This device doesn't feel sluggish at all. Getting to your watch this is as fast as hitting 'home' and then moving up or down from wherever you left off. I can do it in a second. There is also a nice back button so you can navigate backwards. All device should do this. Works perfectly.

Fast Forward

When you are watching a movie, you can fast forward and see a small picture window that gives you a visual preview of the fast forward event. It's really well done. I can quickly find where I want to be and drop off there.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation

text_fidelity_a:
Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100 It takes some getting used to. I have three of these Anker ergos. Two are wireless and are in use at work. One is wired and on my gaming rig at home.

Gaming: My normal mouse is a Logitech gaming mouse which had been my go to for many years. It was fast accurate and had plenty of built in controls for everything I needed. This mouse also has all of the relevant controls and the resolution button is less likely to get accidentally hit than on the Logitech. It does still get hit here and there though. I also find that the vertical style while more comfortable is not as ideal for gaming but honestly speaking is a small niggle in that the comfort is far more appreciated than the slightly awkward hand position (as movements need to be very fast). Is this up to par with other premium gaming controllers? I have my doubts, but it is certainly comfortable and as a wired controller is adequate for sure.

Everyday: Just yes. Especially considering the value. It is both affordable as an ergonomic mouse and comfortable. You may need to make adjustments to your seating angle as the tendency is for this mouse to be most comfortable when your forearm is almost flat on the desk surface.

Look and feel: It is not an especially heavy mouse. But it does have a level of refinement expected on something more costly. It is also well designed and not obscenely gaudy like a lot of products these days. The rubbery matte surface is pleasant and tactile and the buttons are responsive and easy to actuate. The mouse is somewhat full-sized. I don't want to say large because I have small-medium hands and I can use this just fine, but by no means do I have small hands. Those who have small hands might find this more of a challenge to use though I don't doubt you'll get used to it. The primary buttons and grip would be fine, but the locations of the scroll wheel and the forward nav button are a bit of a reach.

Like I said I have three of these in various formats and love them all. Other than my ultra compact travel mouse, these are used on all of my home and work devices. At such a reasonable cost you can't lose by at least trying it.
text_fidelity_b: Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100

text_fidelity_a:
Sennheiser RS 170 Digital Wireless Headphones (Discontinued By Manufacturer) I have owned these headphones since August, 2014. They are easy to use, and the sound quality is excellent. Prior to owning them, I tried out some $20 wireless headphones from a local drugstore which did not work at all, and I also did a jury-rigged setup with a very long, trip-hazard cable linking some headphones I owned to my TiVo. Never again. Both were a disaster.

This system is absolutely wonderful for two reasons:

First, I have weird hearing issues in that when I am trying to sleep, every little sound bugs me and I seem to hear even a conversation in the next room far more clearly than I have any desire to do, but when listening to TV, I can't understand 75% of what the actors are saying without captions. Go figure. With these headphones, no more problem. All dialog is clear as a bell.

Second, I no longer have to drive my husband crazy blaring the TV in order to adequately hear the actors speaking. By the same token, if my husband is watching a program on TV that I'm not at all interested in, I don't have to be subjected to listening to that either.

It's win-win.

I will say that I was not myself techie enough to install these headphones. My husband is an IT guy and he had to do it for me. So that's one downside for the customer who struggles with techie installations. Other than that, all is great.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser RS 170 Digital Wireless Headphones (Discontinued By Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Zune HD 32 GB Video MP3 Player (Platinum) For the past 5 years or so, I've been rocking it out to a Sandisk Sansa. Those were nice little MP3 players, that in my opinion, were superior to the iPod. Well, the Age of the Touch Screen is here, and I wanted an upgrade. The Zune HD seemed like the only solid choice, if I wanted to avoid loading iTunes onto my computer. So I bought one. So far, I think it's a neat little device that gives me *most* of what I want. The sound quality is great, and I like having the internet in my pocket. Microsoft did a fine job with the OS and software; I've had no problems figuring it out. For web capability, it's a bit small, but then again, I appreciate it's size as an MP3 player. I also really like the touch screen. It's nice and responsive, so no problems there, either. Now here's a list of things I'd like to see:

*Micro SD Card slot
*Google Apps
*Netflix (It supports HD vid, so why not Netflix?!)
*Some sort of email client
*Non-proprietary cable for charging.

So far, Microsoft has done a decent job. I'd give it a B+, and I would also feel good about recommending the device to my friends and family.
text_fidelity_b: Zune HD 32 GB Video MP3 Player (Platinum)

Outdoor Tech OT5200 Orcas - Ultra-Light Active Sweat-Proof Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds with Comply Memory Foam Eartips (Black) I live on a farm, so I spend a lot of time outside doing various things. I usually wear a pair of Skullcandy Hesh headphones, but I’m worried that constantly sweating will mean I’ll be replacing them regularly. So I was excited to check out Outdoor Tech’s Orcas, both because they are wireless and because they fit inside the ear. Less sweat all over everything, yay!

Unfortunately, the Orcas were horribly uncomfortable for me. I have small ears, so even the smallest ear tips (there are 3 sizes) were too big. It hurt to have them in for even 5 minutes. I tried them out while doing something that didn’t involve a lot of movement — weeding — and even then they kept falling out of my ears. I had to keep taking my gloves off and forcing them back in my ears. So I can’t imagine how they would stay in for anything more active. The “ear fins” are a neat idea, but again, both pairs are too big for me. I squished them in, but one shake of my head dislodged them.

Another note for the ear fins — if you have any piercings inside your ears, such as a rook or a forward helix, they won’t fit.

I did have trouble pairing the earbuds with my phone, but after tweeting to Outdoor Tech, they set me up with tech support and I had a reply within 10 minutes. (Email is support@outdoortech.com).

The sound quality was okay, nothing super great.

My main issue with the earbuds is just that they’re so uncomfortable! If you have small ears or problems wearing this type of headphones, I’d skip them. I’ll be sticking to my Skullcandys.
text_fidelity_b: Outdoor Tech OT5200 Orcas - Ultra-Light Active Sweat-Proof Wireless Bluetooth Earbuds with Comply Memory Foam Eartips (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th) The Fire HD 10 tablet is pretty much an unbeatable deal for a tablet these days. You get a really good display and decent processor and memory for a great price---especially when it's on sale. And the Fire OS (a rebranded and modified version of Android) works smoothly.

A trade-off is a not-so-good camera resolution.

And there are some limitations on what you can do. If you already own some Android apps, you might not find them in the Amazon app store, and those you do will not credited as paid for. You'll have to buy them again (if you choose to buy).

One option is to follow online instructions for installing the Google Play Store on your Fire. But that's kind of iffy. You don't know when the next Fire OS update might break that installation. And Play Store might download updates to some of the core Fire OS apps that might conflict with proprietary Fire OS modifications.

Another consideration is that this device serves as an advertising and sales platform for Amazon. It's tailored for that. Something to keep in mind.

The thing to consider is if you can be happy with what Amazon gives you. If you're going to be trying to root and work around the OS and app store limitations soon after you get it, maybe it's worth just getting an Android tablet and foregoing the Fire.

If you can be happy with all that, overall it's a great deal for a capable tablet.
text_fidelity_b: Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th)

ZAGG InvisibleShield HD – EZ Apply Film Screen Protector for Apple iPad Air/iPad Air 2 - Wet Apply, Clear TL;DR— not worth the extra cost, it will break and the lifetime warranty is a scam (website doesn’t work, always out of stock), just order a cheaper one and replace— IF you can somehow get Zagg to honor the warranty they will charge you at least $7 to send you a new one when this breaks (and it will def. break)

This was a great screen protector for the several months it lasted before cracking. That partially justifies the steep price tag compared to other screen protectors— but not really.

After I purchased this from amazon I registered this product on the Zagg website, which is necessary to potentially claim a replacement through the “lifetime” warranty program. When it broke, I logged back into their website to order a replacement. The first thing that was annoying was they had a message saying any product ordered within a several years long period would need to be re-registered after they had redesigned their website— my screen protector did not fall into this category, but I assume many people were out of luck on their warranties since they probably no longer had their receipts from screen protectors they had already registered. There was no email or anything warning consumers of this issue, although it’s possible it went out to only the affected people.

When I tried to order a replacement for my broken screen protector I got an error message telling me to try again later. Then the screen protector was out of stock. Then the website is down for maintenance. Then it was out of stock again. The Zagg screen protector on my phone is also broken and also had a warranty. Between the two I have been unable to order a replacement despite trying many, many times. I‘m not a computer engineer or anything, but my computer literacy is usually sufficient to navigate consumer websites. I’m pretty sure the issue is not with me, and if I am doing something wrong it’s because they have intentionally made their website impossible to navigate.

Eventually I gave up and just replaced the screen protector on my phone with a cheaper one. I was able to buy 2 new screen protectors for the same price as the SHIPPING for what the warranty replacement for the Zagg screen protector would have been if it was ever in stock when their website was working, and the difference in quality is negligible.

I don’t appreciate paying extra for a warranty that is not honored and having my time wasted trying to order a replacement when it’s clearly designed to be impossible. I also ended up keeping a broken screen protector on my phone and iPad for months while trying over and over again to order my replacement since it was under warranty.

text_fidelity_a:
Jiusion Telescope Eyepiece Plossl Eyepiece 32mm with 1.25inch Filter Threaded, Astronomical Telescope Lens 50% FOV increase at this price? This is the lowest priced Plössl I've ever seen and the reason for choosing it. Curiosity.

As a physicist with a too time-consuming career to fool around with optical Garage-a-Tronics projects, it's time for fun. After >40 years, I'd guess 1/3 of my time was in electro-optical systems. My responsibilities included one of the nation's most sophisticated optical design, fabrication, and 50-200 layers of Å thickness vapor deposition coating capability (200 layers is no limit … simply the most I've seen engineered)

You have to give them credit. Chinese optics are extraordinary and have been for 20 years. Asian pricing has wholly changed the marketplace. The crazy low prices have made complex systems affordable to the mass market. Optical grinding facilities remaining in the US are confined to a handful of custom, proto-typing houses run by old-timers with a decidedly different product application than consumer use.

The Plössl eyepiece is quite expensive to manufacture given the nature of the glass, coatings, and its precisely coordinated concave and convex lenses to neutralize internal reflections.

The Plössl has tradeoffs. All optical systems do. For example, Plössl's increased FOV comes with an eye relief confined to 70–80% of focal length.

Lenses are analog. Performance is not binary. 'Lowest price' in optics might be misunderstood. Optics lots begin production targeted at a spec performance that makes a profit. A production lot will yield a normal distribution to spec. On the upper end of the distribution are a few 'blue diamonds' commanding a super premium. Theoretically, 66%, will meet the target spec. Production lots begin life as profitable, spec-centered customers. 7% would be expected to fall short of some spec performance (i.e. start 107% of what you need) … Harvard MBA's demanding perfection in all things except stock value have never come to terms with normal analog distributions in scientific endeavors.

text_fidelity_a:
Google Pixel Slate 12.3-Inch 2 in 1 Tablet Intel Core i5, 8GB RAM, 128GB, Aspect Ratio 3:2 The Pixel Slate is Google's computer of the near future. It is great for some people right now, but not for everyone. Google has had their Android tablets and Chromebooks for many years now. The Pixel Slate combines those two concepts into an evolving platform. The hardware is really great right now with great fit-and-finish, a very sharp colorful screen, very responsive touch sensors, and great sound quality. Battery life is very good (over 10 hours per charge). The software is evolving quickly. Google has already released many updates the Chrome operating system and I expect this to continue.

The main problem with the software is that the Pixel Slate is running two types of apps: Chrome browser web-apps and Android apps. The user interfaces for these two are slightly different, which can lead to user confusion. There are also interoperability problems between the two, which also leads to user confusion. For example, Android apps can share files by just clicking on the share icon. Sharing a file from a web-app to an Android app requires downloading the app to the local file system, then opening the Android app and hunting through the file system to find and open the file. Hopefully one day some kind of automatic sharing mechanism will be implemented. Another confusion is that some web-apps and Android apps have the same name and functionality, but don't work the same. For example, Amazon Kindle has both a web-app and an Android app. If I download a book in the Kindle Android app, the Kindle web-app cannot find it, so I have to remember to use the Kindle Android app.

Who should buy a Pixel Slate? Google initially announced 4 versions of this product: one with a Celeron CPU, one with a Core m3 CPU, one with a Core i5 CPU, and one with a Core i7 CPU. I have the i5 version, which is plenty fast and responsive for anything I'm trying to do (I am not a gamer).

Apparently, the performance of the Celeron version was so bad that product has been cancelled. Prices now range from $800 to $1600, not including accessories like the keyboard or stylus. Even the $800 version is a lot of money, especially when you consider that a very good Chromebook can be had for much less money and that has a built-in keyboard. I have to imagine that the only people who should consider the Pixel Slate instead of a high-end Chromebook are people who will regularly need to use this device as a lightweight tablet. At just a pound or so, the Pixel Slate's tablet mode is much lighter weight and much less bulky than any Chromebook, even those flip-over style Chromebooks. If you can't imagine life without a physical keyboard, then get yourself a good Chromebook instead of the Pixel Slate.

The physical keyboard is not included with the Pixel Slate. Amazon sells a couple of different versions, but both have flaws, as well as very high prices. For now, I'm using a Belkin USB keyboard when I'm using the Pixel Slate at my desk. When I'm on the go, I use the tablet in touch screen mode without a physical keyboard. If a better physical keyboard comes along, I'll rethink this setup.
text_fidelity_b: Google Pixel Slate 12.3-Inch 2 in 1 Tablet Intel Core i5, 8GB RAM, 128GB, Aspect Ratio 3:2

Samsung Electronics UN49KS8000 49-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV (2016 Model) I was hesitant to buy a TV online but went to several local stores and many were out of stock since they were transitioning to 2017 models. So I decided to try Amazon on this 2016 Samsung that had many good reviews and was a good price. I was very impressed with both the TV and the delivery from Amazon.
Delivery: I was able to select which day I wanted it delivered and then was kept updated on the delivery status by Amazon. The delivery company called a few days in advance to verify a 3 hour window of time, and they did arrive that day within the window of time even though it was 10 min prior to the end of that time. They brought the TV in, removed it from the boxing, placed it on our TV stand, plugged it in and verified it was functioning. They took a picture of the functioning TV and took the old box/trash away. I was very pleased with the delivery.
The TV: It is great! Have only used the TV for four days but it has been used a lot during that timeframe. We replaced an older Samsung flatscreen (HD TV) with this one and wow, what a difference. Out of the box without any tuning whatsoever this is a great looking deep colored screen. With a few tweaks it is amazing. There were easy step-by-step onscreen setup instructions. The remote is lot better than the older large clunky devices and is a smart remote that even recognizes voice commands. I liked the concept of having just one cable to the TV which then links to a hub where you plug in other devices. Only issue I had was the TV remote could not recognize my Tivo device from my cable provider for all functions, but it did change channels and volume. Trezor Model T - Advanced Crypto Hardware Wallet with LCD Touchscreen, Secure Bitcoin & Over 1450 Coins for Maximum Security I've used a lot of Trezor Ones over the years so I'm really comfortable with the Trezor name and their uses as a hardware wallet. Their reputation is great and the open source nature of their product has set the bar for a lot of competition.

The model T is a marked improvement over the Trezor One. The model T has support for Shamir Secret Sharing which allows you to easily split your recovery seed into multiple parts. The color screen and size also allow for more things to be displayed and verified on the Trezor T. This makes inputs on the device a lot easier than it's predecessor. i.e. when you are inputting or checking a recovery seed or pin, it is a tedious process on the One and very easy to do on the Model T.

The only downside to the Model T is the price. It seems expensive and the build quality could be better. Something about the plastic casing and shape makes it seem cheap. The small screen in comparison to other products make it also seem cheap. For example, Cobo Vault Pro costs approx $150 and has a much larger touch screen and better overall build construction; look and feel wise. At $165 for the model T, the build quality seems very different.

Would I buy another Model T? If the price point were around $100 I would definitely buy many more model Ts. As it is, with a price point of $165, I have opted to buy other competing hardware wallets, Cobo Vault, ColdCard, etc. as I don't think the price to value is quite right for the Model T.

Amazon Basics Full Motion Articulating TV Wall Mount Bracket with Swivel and Tilt Features for 32-80 inch TVs and Flat Panels up to 130 Lbs, Black First of all, I'm looking at reviews and pictures of other peoples item and it seems they have a different item, and yet all the reviews are together. Let me start with the good...

PROS_ Inexpensive!

Cons_

THE INSTRUCTIONS: they are written in 6 different languages, and it jumps back and forth between them. It's not broken English, but very hard to follow. Some of them even have a sort of thumbnail of an entire page of text compressed into about 1.5." It is very bizarre. It took about 30 minutes of studying the pictures to figure out what the heck to do, because the manual certainly doesn't tell you. The box comes with sooo much extra hardware to account for different sizes and mounting situations, but the manual does not explain this well.

THE HARDWARE: It is super heavy duty and weighs nearly as much as my TV. My TV is super light weight and is probably 8 or 9 lbs. The bolts that screw into the stud could hold 100lbs I'm sure. Even pre-drilling pilot holes I had difficulty screwing them in with a drill they are so big. It takes so much torque that the screws stripped. I ended up using 1.5" wood screws. I used a stud and I don't like where the TV is mounted, so I am going to get molly bolts to screw it into the drywall where I would like to put it.

NOT STURDY: You mount a plate to the back of the TV, then you mount another piece of hardware to the wall. You then attach the TV to the hardware you just attached to the wall. It is wobbly. It also tilts anywhere from a perfectly neutral position to 20 degree or so angle down. This is in case you are mounting it very high and wish to tilt it down. The TV keeps flopping forward and tilting down. There is a bolt that keeps it in place and I tightened the heck out of it, and it just barely stays put.

NOT FLUSH: I have no other mounting systems to compare it to, but the TV sticks out about 2.5" from the wall. I was expecting it to be much closer.

So there you have it. I am not happy. Ultimately I have the mounted now and no real reason to return it because it's doing what I need it to. There are a lot of positive reviews, but they are I'm sure for a different product. Anyways I paid $15.95. You will most likely be happier with something you pay $25 for.

I included photos of the manual. You can see how the TV mounts, all the extra hardware, as well as a few pages of horrible manual- complete with the mini thumbnail pages.

Samsung Electronics 840 EVO-Series 120GB 2.5-Inch SATA III Single Unit Version Internal Solid State Drive MZ-7TE120BW This is my second SSD, my first being a Kingston (with the Taiwan firmware thank God) so I thought install was going to be fairly easy; it was not. My system (Win7) did not recognize the drive, but the included software, Samsung Magician, said the drive was there, operating properly, but was "frozen". I googled the malfunction and found out that the drive had no partitions.

So first step was to get in Disk Management, find the drive, click on the 113+gb unallocated space and create a partition.

Step two, reboot and change my boot sequence because Samsung Magician felt it was necessary to change it for me and made this new SSD my boot drive, even though it had no OS on it to boot.

Step three, change my power management plan back to what I had before because Samsung Magician felt it was better to change it to hibernate instead of what I wanted. I hate Hibernate.

After that it worked great. I use this SSD for games only because it's so damn fast, but I wish the included software and instructions were better, hence the 4 stars and not 5.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Electronics 840 EVO-Series 120GB 2.5-Inch SATA III Single Unit Version Internal Solid State Drive MZ-7TE120BW

SABRENT 9U IT Wall Mount Rack Enclosure 19 Inch Black Server Cabinet with Locking Glass Door - Fully Assembled (CT-DSWL) The shipping packaging was not enough to prevent some minor damage . Fortunately, it was just cosmetic dents on some of the corners. (see picture)
The mounting holes were 16 inches apart so perfect for lining up with the studs in my wall. I would have liked some better mounting hardware. I believe that it will hold the listed 88-pound max weight.
As with all wall mount racks the depth of the rack is limited. There is about an inch and half clearance from the front brackets and glass door. I would not want to use any CAT6 patch cables in patch panels or switches on the front brackets. The back has about three and half inches clearance.
It comes with punchouts at the rear of the rack on top and bottom. This provides plenty of cable access.
Air flow and heat buildup is my biggest concern. If you have anything that generates a large amount of heat you will need to add fans for the very limited air holes. I would have preferred a screen for the front door and many more holes in the top of the rack. I was easily able to remove both sides and the front door. This is going to be my solution as I add more equipment.
The lock on the front door and the rear hinge is there to keep honest people honest. After I started installing equipment in the rack I was hesitant to open the hinge to access the back.
I am happy with the value for the price. For a low heat installation or if you are willing to remove the sides, it makes a nice small office or home rack.
text_fidelity_b: SABRENT 9U IT Wall Mount Rack Enclosure 19 Inch Black Server Cabinet with Locking Glass Door - Fully Assembled (CT-DSWL)

text_fidelity_a:
Inateck 3.5 Hard Drive Enclosure, Aluminum USB 3.0 Sata HDD Enclosure, FE3001 I've had this enclosure for almost 2 years. My five year old computer was very slow and I was having lots of trouble with it and the enclosure connecting to it. I did get it to connect and do one backup, but that was it. So, I thought surely it was my pc that was the problem. It would either not connect or it would not do anything...like I didn't have it plugged in. I just thought all three connections had to be made properly for it to come on and do it's job. I am not completely tech stupid, nor savvy.
I am disabled, so I was saving for a new computer. I have had lots of sickness over this time, and getting to this was not a huge priority and I never came back to read reviews. I wish I had.
I finally did recently get a new pc, and just the other day wanted to give it another go. When I plugged it in, again, there seemed to be no power... and then suddenly there was a burning smell and smoke coming from the enclosure where the power supply went in. It was quite scary, because I almost did not catch it soon enough.
I took a long shot and contacted the company anyways, even though it had been such a while to explain the long ordeal, and why I had not contacted sooner... Among my sickness, I was giving the device the benefit of the doubt, because I honestly thought it was my pc.
This is the message I received in return "In this case, it is highly commended to stop using this hard drive enclosure.
According to your information, this item is faulty. Regarding our products, a 12-month warranty is provided, however, it is obviously that the item ordered on 2016 has been far beyond its warranty. Hope that you could understand."
They did offer a 15% "return after purchase" discount refund if I would purchase a new one. But, as I am disabled, I cannot afford to do that at this time.
Hopefully, my backup really is on the hard drive that this unit supposedly saved it to that one time, as some beloved photos of my deceased father are on there, and I don't have them anywhere else.
I wish I were more tech savvy and didn't stay sick so much... Even so, I wouldn't have known the problem until I got a new pc anyways. Based on my experience and other reviews, I would not recommend this enclosure to anyone.
I do hope this helps someone.
text_fidelity_b: Inateck 3.5 Hard Drive Enclosure, Aluminum USB 3.0 Sata HDD Enclosure, FE3001

Cooler Master Hyper 212 EVO V2 CPU Air Cooler with SickleFlow 120, PWM Fan, Direct Contact Technology, 4 Copper Heat Pipes for AMD Ryzen/Intel LGA1700/1200/1151, Silver/Black Boy is this big. Fortunately it fits just barely in my Sentey Gaming case. I had purchased the Arctic Freezer 7 Pro Rev 2 but that was far worse than the AMD 8350's included cooler fan, probably because the contact surface is designed for Intel chips and is much smaller than for AMD chips.
Be prepared for some work installing this fan as you have to install a new back-plate on the motherboard. The included parts are perfect in that they provide everything you will need including the thermal compound. So I also purchased the 2 top case fans (Corsair series). Without the cooler, the top fans did indeed reduce the top CPU temperatures by about 4C degrees - almost as though the case cover is open. With the cooler though the CPU temperature never climbed beyond 61C degrees even when all 8 cores were saturated (was compiling code). Without the cooler and the the top fans I was hitting 70C degrees which is 5 degrees above allowed operating temperature. I am surprised my AMD 8350 is still operational. With the cooler and top fans the temperature drop is 15C which is a win! Maybe I can use the Arcrtic Freezer in an Intel setup.

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire One Cloudbook, 11-Inch HD, 32GB, Windows 10, Gray (AO1-131-C9PM) includes Office 365 Personal – 1 year **Discontinued by Manufacturer** There's a lot of reviews already about this product. I wavered for a good while about deciding if I wanted to accept this Cloudbook for review and now kind of wish I hadn't. As far as I'm concerned, the Cloudbook is like a merging of a laptop and a chromebook with neither giving the features that are special to each one. As far as it being a computer, it runs on Windows 10 of which I have great suspicions and doubts. If you remember, I believe most everyone received an offer for a free download of Windows 10 as an upgrade from whatever Windows program they were currently using. I have read from several sources that it was offered only as a way of installing NSA spyware on your computer. We are being watched and monitored at every turn. If you don't believe me, next time you are driving take a look at all the cameras on poles along the roads and highways and tell me we aren't being surveilled. Smartphones, smart TV's, smart refrigerators, dryers and washing machines are simply ways of letting TPTB know what we are doing at all times. How many loads of clothes you washed, what you are doing in your bedroom and on and on. So, what does all this have to do with this little and cute computer? It has Windows 10 installed.

If you are o.k. with that then overall it's not a bad machine. I really miss having a disk drive to load my own personal programs and don't like having to download stuff from the internet via the app store or some other internet source. And since it is a computer but has very little space for storage, you have to have an anti-virus program. It comes with one but it's only good for 30 days and you have to purchase it or get another one. Most of your stuff will be stored in the Cloud (like a chromebook) unless you opt for a Sandisk or external hard drive. And if you buy an external hard drive for more storage why not get a regular computer instead that has more bells and whistles and possibly a disk drive?

It looks like a chromebook and I have had to put a label on it to distinguish it from mine and my kids chromebooks. I'm having a hard time getting used to Windows 10 and it takes a long time to finally get on the internet. I have taped a piece of paper over the camera lens staring me in the face - call me paranoid if you wish but I don't like people in my house uninvited. The "shift" key is way too small and I'm always missing it.

As far as specs go they're listed on the main page but here they are again for your convenience:

11.6" HD Widescreen ComfyView LED-backlit Display (1366 x 768 resolution, 16:9 aspect ratio).
Intel Celeron N3050 Dual-Core Processor 1.6GHz with Intel Burst Technology up to 2.16GHz.
Windows 10
Intel HD Graphics
2GB of DDR3L Onboard Memory.
32GB Internal Storage
Secure Digital (SD) card reader.
802.11ac WiFi (Dual-Band 2.4GHz and 5GHz).
Bluetooth 4.0
Webcam (640 x 480)
High-definition audio support.
Two Built-in Stereo Speakers.
1 - USB 3.0 port
1 - USB 2.0 port
1 - HDMI Port with HDCP support.
Microsoft Office 365 Personal 1-Year Subscription (activation code included).
2-cell Li-polymer battery pack (4200mAh).
Up to 8 hours of battery life (Video Playback).
2.54 lbs. | 1.15kg (system unit only).

If you are already using Windows 10 then it should be easy to navigate, but I feel as if I'm learning a whole new OS though I use Windows 8 on my other laptop. It only detected two of my Bluetooth devices and I have several. If you want Word processing you must redeem your card number inside the box before a certain date or else it expires. And it's all cloud based so your data is out there and not in your pc safe and sound.

I will modify this review as needed, but I have not used this computer since a few days ago and probably will not be using it much at all. I like my chromebook better for web surfing, and it doesn't require an anti-virus program because it's totally cloud based but I never use the cloud. I store the stuff I want on my old desktop or other laptop. And my chromebook has access to a word processing program without having to buy it.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire One Cloudbook, 11-Inch HD, 32GB, Windows 10, Gray (AO1-131-C9PM) includes Office 365 Personal – 1 year **Discontinued by Manufacturer**

text_fidelity_a:
Behringer MICROAMP HA400 Ultra-Compact 4 Channel Stereo Headphone Amplifier,Silver After an attempt to use [[ASIN:B005INJ4ZG My Zone Wireless Headphones]] was a bust for me due to its terrible sound quality, my techie husband bought this amp for me as part of a setup that allows me to listen to TV as loud as I want without disturbing him or the neighbors.

I directly hook up this amp to a head phone or earbuds when I am sitting close to the TV by using a special [[ASIN:B00009UVPN adapter]]. Head phones and earbuds have a 1/8 inch (3.5 mm) male jack (AKA male connector). Without an adapter, they can't be inserted into this amp, whose plug (AKA socket, female jack, or female connector) measures 1/4 inch (6.35 mm).

Because I like to move around my living room when I am watching TV, my husband also bought me a special [[ASIN:B0010CX798 male-to-female, headphone adapter, extension cable]]. The 1/4-inch, male jack of this cable fits into the 1/4-inch plug of this amp, and it has a 1/8-inch plug on its other end into which the jack of a head phone or ear bud can fit.

In order to use this setup, my husband also hooked into this amp a [[ASIN:B000068O3F male-to-male extension cable]]; one end is 1/8-inch and the other is 1/4-inch in diameter. The smaller end fits into a plug on the TV. When I want to use this external speaker source, I use the TV remote to access a menu that allows me to do that. Once this system is hooked up, I can no longer adjust the sound volume on the TV itself. I use the volume control on this amp.

Note that there is no On/Off switch on this amp. If you want to turn it off, so that you are not wasting electricity when it is not in use, you unhook the power cord from the far-left side of the amp.

This setup is a little complicated for the non-techie to figure out on their own, but if you have anyone techie in your family who can do it for you, it works really well.
text_fidelity_b: Behringer MICROAMP HA400 Ultra-Compact 4 Channel Stereo Headphone Amplifier,Silver

ETUCRAY Headphone Jack Adapter for Phone Dongle Aux Audio to 3.5mm Cables Earphone Adaptor Headset Splitter for Music&Charger This timer is a good size with a very readable LED display and a strong magnet on the clip on the back to hold it to your fridge or whatever a magnet will stick to. The buttons are large and accessible, and it's really no problem to set it up. It beeps loudly when the time is up, so there's little danger you're not going to hear it from an adjoining room.

Strangely, on day one (unlike with some timers I've used), the first three or four times that I held down the hour, minute, or second buttons to speed up the counting and turn off the beeps, it just froze and stopped counting. If I pressed the button over and over to advance the counter by one, it worked—beeping annoyingly loudly each time, of course. I was about to give it a two-star review and throw it away because I couldn't stand it, but I put off doing it and just stuck it to the top of my stove. A week later, after I'd used the stove several times and the timer probably got exposed to some heat, I went back to try it again so I could write this review and the fast-count sans beeps feature worked. Weird. Maybe it was just stressed in shipping and needed time to settle down....

A few things I really do dislike is that it's easy to reset the time by mistake if the grey button on the left gets slid up; the modes are manually set with this button. (That approach to the modes could be good for the technologically challenged, though.) Also, if you overshoot your mark on the time, there is no way to go backward; you have to go forward until you come back around to where you were supposed to have stopped the first time. The clip is a little too sharply angled, so when you stick the timer to a surface with the magnet, the face slants down somewhat, but it's still visible; really not that big of a deal.

Another thing, as I've remarked about another MeasuPro product: the how-to info on the packaging is white letters on light grey, which is practically unreadable for anyone, not just people like me with old eyes. (The company told me they were correcting that with the other product, so I expect they will do the same with this one.)
text_fidelity_b: ETUCRAY Headphone Jack Adapter for Phone Dongle Aux Audio to 3.5mm Cables Earphone Adaptor Headset Splitter for Music&Charger

Belkin 6-Outlet Surge Protector with 3-Foot Cord (Plus An Extra 6-Foot Extension Cord) I'm confused. I thought when I got this surge suppressor that the extension cord was meant to be used with it so you'd have a total of nine feet of cord if needed. Apparently, the extension cord doesn't actually fit the surge suppressor; the extension cord has three two-prong receptacles that you could plug, say, lamps and the like into, but you cannot plug the surge suppressor itself into it. The extension cord is clearly marked as being for two-wire polarized, as opposed to three-prong grounded, appliances. So that's more than a little misleading.

The surge suppressor looks heavy-duty, but you are cautioned in the packaging literature that it's not to be used with "sensitive equipment" like everything we use surge suppressors for: computers, TV, etc. You can't use it with things involving water, either, like aquariums. So what would I use it for? A blow dryer? I think not. To make it even worse, you are told to cover the receptacles on the extension cord if they are not in use. There are little plastic sliders that you're supposed to use for this purpose. But one of the sliders on the extension cord I received won't stay closed. China-cheap.

Belkin has some good products, but this one doesn't impress me very much. And the whole thing is packaged in one of those awful clamshells that you risk hurting yourself on when you take the scissors to it.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin 6-Outlet Surge Protector with 3-Foot Cord (Plus An Extra 6-Foot Extension Cord)

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm FinePix Z90 14 MP Digital Camera with Fujinon 5x Wide Angle Optical Zoom Lens and 3-Inch Touch-Screen LCD (Red) This camera is what I call a "subcompact" - the smallest point and shoot cameras that have vertically mounted lenses which allow protection, compactness, and quicker start up times. Normally, you'd expect a small trade off for these features, so I wouldn't compare this directly with a camera endowed by a telescoping lens.

Sony invented the subcompact with the T1 a few years back (at least in my world), and I was able to compare the FinePix Z90 with the one-generation-older 12 MP Sony T90. I'll go the pro/con route...

PROS of the Z90:

-Price is something like half of the latest subcompact Sony.
-Operational costs are cheaper: USB cable is non-proprietary (in case you want a second one or need to replace it) and SD card is cheaper and more universal than Sony's Memory Stick.
-Separate physical buttons to record movies and to take pictures. This is genius to me, because I hate to miss a great video opportunity while fumbling through the menus.
-Does not come with a memory card, BUT cameras that do usually come with one so small that it is worthless. Internal memory is better, because it allows you to copy from one camera card to another, which can be useful.
-Can set it up to take two photos at once, with and without the flash. As an amateur, I often do this manually anyway, but this way you get closer photos (chronologically)to compare in a dynamic scenario, and the subject needs only to pose once.
-The panorama mode works better than in other cameras I've used. They use internal weights alla smart phones (I'm guessing) to help you line up the next picture. Allows you to "pan" a panorama shot in play mode.
-There is a time zone mode that allows you to temporarily change the time (for timestamps).
-The display changes from horizontal to vertical as you move the camera respectively.
-"Touch and track" mode follows a subject.
-Side by side picture compare.
-Search by face, couple, group, favorites, scene, or date, and view a small picture next to thumbnails.
-Charger is smaller with the plug offset to allow it to use only one receptacle on a power strip (as long as it is at the end of said strip).

CONS of the Z90:

-Picture quality was not as good as the Sony 80% of the time (tested in various modes and lighting conditions). That said, a tripod really helps with low light and no flash, where both cameras struggle without it.
-By numbers, it is not much larger than the Sony, but it feels significantly larger.
-Sometimes the "buttons" in the corners of the touch screen need to be pressed more than once.
-Tripod mount has plastic threads, instead of a machined metal insert.
-Cannot take shots as rapidly as on the Sony
-Does not tell you what zoom level you are at. 5x zoom does not appear to make a great difference over 4x.
-"play" and "camera" buttons could be one button used as a toggle.
-Battery can be put in backward, as the slot is not keyed (although the battery is). No big deal, but shows something wasn't thought out thoroughly.

Bottom Line:

The Fuji is trying to deliver everything the market leader has to offer for a much more manageable price tag. It gets an A for effort, delivering a lot of great menu options, and may actually win in that respect, but the picture quality is not as good. If they could pour a little more money into the actual optics and the touch screen and still keep the price reasonable, they might win the battle in the future. For now, it's purely a personal budget vs. quality decision.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm FinePix Z90 14 MP Digital Camera with Fujinon 5x Wide Angle Optical Zoom Lens and 3-Inch Touch-Screen LCD (Red)

text_fidelity_a:
AKG (A Samsung Brand) N700NC M2 Over-Ear Foldable Wireless , Active Noise Cancelling Headphones - Black (US Version), 2.6, Model:GP-N700HAHCIWA Ok I can be a bit of a headphone snob, but at a near $300 price point I have some pretty high expectations. I ran them through my standard audio tests and these passed every one with flying colors. Bottomline, where most wireless sets fail is with bass, either its lacking or they overcompensate for it at the expense of everything else. (I'm talking to you SkullCandy). These however managed to be astounding on bass without it being overwhelming. Deep rich sounds, but mid and upper still came in crystal clear. It was impressive.

They also manage to have noise canceling without the annoying hiss present in the high end SkullCandy set I recently reviewed. The AKG's are superior and even performed better than my beloved, but admittedly old Sennheisers. How they would match up against a newer pair I can't say though, I will fangirl all day over a high end set of Senn's, but these AKGs give them some serious competition.

The ambient pass-through was a welcome addition, and these paired effortlessly via blue tooth. The ear cups were comfortable, although warm like every other pair of closed noise-canceling headsets I've tried. I will be honest I tend to prefer an open headset, but that is more preference than anything to do with this set. The ear cups were smaller than other pairs I've worn, I'm petite so that wasn't an issue but if you got yourself some good sized ears keep that in mind.

So if you have $300 burning a hole in your pocket and need some very well balanced wireless headphones, I highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: AKG (A Samsung Brand) N700NC M2 Over-Ear Foldable Wireless , Active Noise Cancelling Headphones - Black (US Version), 2.6, Model:GP-N700HAHCIWA

TOZO T6 True Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth 5.3 Headphones Touch Control with Wireless Charging Case IPX8 Waterproof Stereo Earphones in-Ear Built-in Mic Headset Premium Deep Bass White (2022 Upgraded) I own the TOZO T10, and I can't say enough great things about them, but alas, I stupidly left one where the puppy could get it, and now I have one ear that still performs, but the 'button' no longer works (amazing that it didn't break).

I probably should have bought another pair of the T10s, but the T6s had pretty amazing specs, so I took a chance.

First, the pros; AMAZING sound, noise isolation, fit, and sensitive fingerprint controls (no pressing). I have over ear Bose, and Beats, and these could stand against their sound quality any day.

Now the cons: you can't roam far from the phone, computer or iPad you're connected to, or the bluetooth will drop you. In fact, if a butterfly farts in the amazon, these earbuds will drop their connection to your bluetooth device. The other stand-out con is battery life. I don't know if mine were defective, but they NEVER had the battery that I enjoyed with the T10s, and they seem to be getting worse. The case will hold a charge when stored for well over a week, but the buds last about four hours with music playing in them. If you're just wearing them at the gym for an hour or two, they're fine, but if you're wearing them to drown out office noise, you're going to be out of luck after lunch.

I am considering handing these off to one of the younger people in my family who need a spare pair to use while their primary pair is charging. If TOZO comes out with a new model, I may wait to see if the folks reviewing it have the same issues. I'm actively looking for the old T10s in the meantime.
text_fidelity_b: TOZO T6 True Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth 5.3 Headphones Touch Control with Wireless Charging Case IPX8 Waterproof Stereo Earphones in-Ear Built-in Mic Headset Premium Deep Bass White (2022 Upgraded)

text_fidelity_a:
Philips BT2500B/37 Wireless Portable Speaker I have owned those annoying bluetooth ear pieces that always feel like they're about to fall off - or actually do. And although the sound varies from product to product, it's just not a system I am comfortable with.

This little speaker is simply perfect for my needs. It is 4 inches by 4 inches wide and only 1 inch thick. It has a switch that you slide to the right when you wish to enable the bluetooth, or to the left to turn it off. There is also another small button right beside the switch that you push in to receive or disconnect a call. A silver volume knob is sleekly incorporated in the overal design. The pairing was instant and consistant. No need to type in some code or wait forever for them to find each other. But here's the most important part - I hear my calls clearly and with no drop off or fade.

In all fairness, I only use this in my car and I don't spend ridiculous amounts of time on my phone when I'm driving. I've used other products with useless results. Half of the time I would risk a ticket by just ditching the ear piece and talking on my cell. In this case, I'm able to place it on the seat next to me and converse without any problems. Now that it's passed my tests, I'll be getting some velcro and mounting it to my dash board when I'm driving, and then just popping it in the glove compartment when I'm done.

The unit comes with a USB charger cable and it had a partial charge when I received it. Once it's fully charged and you turn it on, a blue light will blink for about 2 seconds and then go to a solid blue. According to the enclosed instructions, you will know that the battery is low when it blinks red. Couldn't be easier.

Musically speaking, my JBL and Sony are better designed for that purpose. But as a compact, speaker phone - this Phillips is without equal. Hands-free clarity without an annoying piece of plastic hanging over your ear. What more could you ask?
text_fidelity_b: Philips BT2500B/37 Wireless Portable Speaker

Belkin Verve Folio Case with Stand for Samsung Galaxy Tab 10.1inch (Black) My favorite types of cases are the rigid style that grab onto the edges of the device and do not increase the width or length of the device significantly. This is sort of a hybrid between that style and Belkin's ultrathin folio style.

That's because this one has a "pocket" for the device just like the soft ultrathins, which means you see the screen through a well placed cutout. It also has holes cut for the buttons, lenses, and ports. It is smaller from a length and width perspective than the ultrathin, but a bit deeper because the cover is thicker. It also has cleaner lines, although not as clean as some hard cases.

It also has an elastic strap attached to the cover that can be turned around to hold the case shut. Only time will tell if that stays nice and tight or ends up sagging after use. Really, it doesn't need to be used often as the case will mostly stay shut by itself.

The one thing I don't like is the way you fold the front cover behind the back: it sort of seems too stiff, as if you're not really supposed to. It also folds at both joints, which keeps it from lying completely flat. The ultrathin folio has it beat in that case, although I like the Verve in better in most other ways.

A nice case for your tablet.

Seagate Expansion Desktop 12TB External Hard Drive HDD - USB 3.0 for PC Laptop (STEB12000400) The perfect external 3.5" hard drive for purchase at this point in time as far as I'm concerned: they include controller software *if you want it*, but they don't try to persuade you to use it, instead taking the simplistic approach, which is plug it in and use it! I would never use software to run a hard drive anyway.

Also, 4TB seems to be the sweet spot right now for price/size ratio for external 3.5" storage (3.5" drives always require an external power source, whereas 2.5" external drives - which are sometimes slower - usually do not). I like that you can leave it plugged in, but it only powers on when you attach the USB cable.

USB 3.0 really is a vast improvement over previous versions. I'm dumping all my files from five other drives on this monster, and 500GB are transferring through the computer from one drive to another in around 2-3 hours, both large and tiny files.

Worth noting is that the case seems very thin around the drive, which is probably good for heat dispersion, but will not provide the kind of protection you'd want if you were constantly transporting this drive.

I now have on here hundreds of seasons of TV shows, most in HD, nearly a thousand movies, most in HD, hundreds of music albums, books, maps, comics, software setup files, etc., and I STILL have room to grow. To get all these things consolidated and organized - and all accessible with a single drive powered up - is really fantastic.
text_fidelity_b: Seagate Expansion Desktop 12TB External Hard Drive HDD - USB 3.0 for PC Laptop (STEB12000400)

text_fidelity_a:
RCA RD1006 Discwasher D4+ Vinyl Record Care System This is the best record cleaning I tried so far. I is very effective in removing dust (and associated static noise) from records that are in reasonably good shape. Of course, it cannot repair records which have been damaged due to being played while dirty. If you acquire a used record in dirty condition, it is probably a good idea to wash it with distilled water first before using the discwasher on it.

I noticed that there are several one-star reviews complaining about the direction of fibers on the cleaning pad that comes with this system. Yes, the cords of the corduroy-like microfiber material does run along the edge of the brush, but this is actually how it should be to provide even coverage across all the grooves. The cords of any fabric is much too thick to fit into the actual grooves on the record. If the cords were to run along the direction of the the grooves, some grooves would be cleaned and some wouldn't. Having the cords being perpendicular to the grooves on the record ensures that all grooves get cleaned evenly. After all, it is the microfibers, not the cords of the fabric, doing the cleaning.

Another advantage of cords running perpendicular to the grooves of the record is that, as you slowly rotate the brush on its axis (as shown in the provided directions), dust that has been collected gets trapped between the cords that are being lifted off the record as the next (clean) cord of the fabric starts making contact with the record surface.
text_fidelity_b: RCA RD1006 Discwasher D4+ Vinyl Record Care System

Digital Photo Frame 15-inch WiFi Digital Picture Frame - FULLJA Smart Digital Photo Frames 32GB Storage, Easy to Setup and Share Photos and Videos via App or Email, Gifts for Family The Fullja 10 inch WiFi Digital Picture Frame replaces >5-year-old LCD frame. Wow. Excellent upgrade in both hardware and software.

The total frame size is 10" x 7" in practical terms. The IPS (in-plane switching) touch-screen LCD at 1280x800 resolution (189 PPI) is HD, one LCD grade less than FHD. I can't discriminate between HD and FHD resolution from a picture frame's typical viewing distance. The LCD viewing angle is excellent, consistent with the IPS fabrication. This is important, perhaps THE most important criteria for an LCD picture frame. The LCD's backlighting is motion-activated and quite good. Backlighting consumes most of the battery current. Motion detection will extend battery life.

Clock, calendar, and weather update options expand the utility beyond a picture frame. Image connectivity and control include the range from TF portable memory to WiFi. Very cool.

Better than expected. Excellent value for money. One wonders how it can be made at the price.

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Show (2nd Gen) | Premium 10.1” HD smart display with Alexa – stay connected with video calling - Sandstone 👸My house is, and will probably forever be, owned by Alexa!👸
First, let me say, that I bought the Echo 2nd Generation, and the Google Hub at the very same time, just to try them both out. And boy, I could not send that Google Hub back to where it came from fast enough! It may be great for smart home only users, but it is no fun or really that useful, other than that, at all! You cannot even get answers or videos that come even close to what Google gives you on your cell phone!! And, it is not for the sight impaired- meaning me. If I needed to know the time after 6pm, I asked Alexa. I don't get it...
And, oh yeah baby! I love lyric mode on this thing! This bad boy can rock your booty off, for sure! The bass vibrates everything on my kitchen counter! I love it!!
I call mine Alexxx sometimes... it answers, most of the time, no matter which name- Alexa or Alexxx. I do wish it had a man's voice, sometimes.... really could use hearing one once in a while! It's kinda funny, sometimes, I just get ignored- similar to a man lol. Like, when I asked her to repeat the same song for the tenth time. Or, she will just decide that I need to listen to a certain playlist, instead of said song. It's annoying, but sometimes the first song is so good, it gets me to listen. Still... If I say play this song, and she says, I'll play "this" instead, it's rude!
Another thing I absolutely love, is watching YouTube. I've saved my Channel to the homepage in the Silk Browser, so all I have to do is just tell it to open YouTube. It goes straight to my homepage. I can go to or watch my subscription feed and playlists, go to my watched history, watch recommended videos, and easily search for anything I would like to watch. It is so quick and easy to navigate! My most favorite thing to watch, is Criminal trials, and they last for weeks. So, while I'm working in the kitchen doing other things, or just sitting around the table, I can pick up where I left off on my Fire Stick, and watch them right there on my echo.
I can search the internet for anything! I can type it in, or make it even faster by using my voice and just hitting the enter key on the onscreen keyboard.
I've heard a lot of people complain that there are too many steps to do things on the Echo. But, I can get to anywhere on mine almost as quickly as I can on my regular computer.
I hate to say that I haven't ventured out into the many, many things this thing can do, other than these few things, but they're the ones that I enjoy. One day, I'll try venturing out into unchartered territory for myself on this lovely device.
I know I can tell you one thing is for certain. I will definitely be buying more of these wonderful, booty shaking, singing to the top of my lungs, mind blowing gadgets very soon! I just have to have them in several rooms! I highly, highly, highly recommend the Echo 2nd Generation to everyone! REALLY, EVERYONE!!
text_fidelity_b: Echo Show (2nd Gen) | Premium 10.1” HD smart display with Alexa – stay connected with video calling - Sandstone

text_fidelity_a:
Sony WF-1000XM4 Industry Leading Noise Canceling Truly Wireless Earbud Headphones with Alexa Built-in, Black This product feels different to me than other Sony stuff I've gotten. It's like they've gone out of their way to make everything feel like cardboard. The packaging was like egg carton, and the earbuds and their charging station are a rough lightweight material in a drab color. The earbuds themselves are customizable, but bulky compared to the competition. I find them hard to get out of the container, hard to hold onto, and hard to wear. The noise cancellation and sound are both above average though. I like the charging light on the container. It communicates with color and flashes what the status of the product is, and isn't bright or hard to locate.

USB-C charging makes the base station charge up nice and fast. It holds the earbuds securely, and doesn't rattle or fall open. It's also a nice pocketable size and shape with no sharp corners, making the whole product especially portable. Controls are gesture, rather than button. I'm not a fan of this because I end up doing a lot of swiping and hoping. A click button interface, I can just click it the number of times I know will do what I need, and move on.

I've got a few Sony audio products that I use every day and am very happy with, but with earbuds, I'm sticking with jabra for now. It's a competitive market right now for earbuds. Lots of companies putting out new designs.
text_fidelity_b: Sony WF-1000XM4 Industry Leading Noise Canceling Truly Wireless Earbud Headphones with Alexa Built-in, Black
